title: Has Democracy Failed to Deliver in Pakistan?
examQuestion: Has Democracy Failed to Deliver in Pakistan?
description: Controversial two-sided debate prompt (requiresCounterArgument = true) that commits three classic CSS blunders: (1) omits Counter-Argument/Rebuttal, (2) appends a bureaucratic 'Way Forward' section to a debate prompt, and (3) inserts inline headings inside the essay prose body.
rawText:
Outline
1. Introduction
2. Why Democracy Has Failed in Pakistan
   2.1. Feudal political parties
   2.2. Weak local governments
3. Way Forward to Fix Democracy
   3.1. Electoral reforms
   3.2. Strengthening parliament
4. Conclusion

Introduction
Democracy is a system of government by the whole population or all the eligible members of a state, typically through elected representatives. Since 1947, Pakistan has experimented with parliamentary democracy multiple times, yet ordinary citizens still suffer from poverty, inflation, and weak governance. Therefore, democracy has completely failed to deliver in Pakistan.

Feudal Political Parties
Political parties in Pakistan operate like family fiefdoms rather than democratic institutions. Internal party elections are rarely held with transparency, and tickets are awarded to wealthy electables who prioritize personal patronage over national legislation. Consequently, parliamentary debates focus on partisan mudslinging rather than socioeconomic reform.

Absence of Local Governments
Furthermore, provincial governments routinely resist devolving administrative and financial powers to elected local bodies under Article 140-A of the Constitution. Without empowered municipal councils, citizens remain deprived of clean drinking water, sanitation, and primary healthcare at the grass-roots level.

Way Forward
To make democracy successful, the Election Commission must enforce strict campaign finance limits and mandate regular local body elections across all provinces.

Conclusion
In conclusion, democracy has failed to deliver in Pakistan due to dynastic politics and weak institutions.
